Northern Hardwood Mill Feed Map · Mid-Atlantic v0.6

Where can northern hardwood find a market?

A 5 km heat map of modeled annual offered hardwood supply and public buyer-site access across the northern-hardwood portions of New York, Pennsylvania, and New Jersey. Switch products to reveal where a healthy sawlog channel can coexist with a pulpwood, veneer, or residue gap.

Screening evidence, not observed procurement

Heat cells combine TreeMap, NALCMS, and state FIA growth controls with explicit offer and product-basket assumptions. Buyer links use straight-line distance to public evidence sites. Mill intake, utilization, price, willingness to procure, and truck routes remain unobserved.

      How to read the heat

      Warm cells contain modeled pulpwood supply with no confirmed compatible public buyer site inside a 150 km straight-line screen. A cold color is a signal to investigate, not proof that wood is unmarketable.

      What “confirmed” and “exploratory” mean

      Confirmed retains named independent evidence and public TPO facility classes that directly indicate a compatible processing or intermediary market channel. Concentration and export yards remain intermediary evidence, not final processing capacity. Exploratory also includes composite-panel, energy, mulch, and similar records whose accepted hardwood feedstock form still needs confirmation. Display-only pellet plants never enter buyer counts.

      Limits of v0.6
      • No facility-level intake capacity, utilization, prices, procurement radii, or willingness to buy.
      • No capacity-constrained allocation, delivered margin, or stranded-volume claim.
      • Distances are centroid-to-site straight-line lower bounds, not OSM routes or drive times.
      • Canadian buyers are omitted, so northern New York buyer diversity is a lower bound.
      • TreeMap cells are imputed; the 5 km surface is regional screening evidence, not parcel precision.
      • Hatched cells have below-90% TreeMap coverage or tree-table linkage and use documented fallback information.
      Data and scenario record

      Forest evidence: TreeMap 2023 (RDS-2026-0038), NALCMS 2020 land cover, and common-year 2024 official FIADB-API/EVALIDator state growth controls. Market evidence: public USFS TPO 2023 locations plus independently sourced named pulp, paper, veneer, closure, and pellet evidence. Operability context uses USGS 3DEP, NWI, PAD-US, and OpenStreetMap.

      The “announced/current” view starts from the public 2023 structure and applies only independently documented changes known through August 28, 2026. Unchanged anonymous locations are carried forward from 2023; they were not individually reverified in 2026.
